say.en: Your roll number is 45. How would a computer write it in binary? One simple method, repeated division, gives the answer. In this lesson: Convert a decimal integer to binary, octal and hexadecimal by repeated division.
Convert a decimal fraction to binary by repeated multiplication.

body.en: To convert a *decimal* integer to base b, divide it by b repeatedly and write down each remainder, until the quotient becomes 0. Reading the remainders from the last to the first (bottom to top) gives the number in base b. For hexadecimal, remainders 10 to 15 are written as A to F.

title.en: On the board: Decimal 25 to binary, and 0.625 to binary

say.en: Divide 25 by 2 and write the quotient and the remainder.
Keep dividing the quotient by 2 until it becomes 0.
Read the remainders from the bottom to the top. So 25 is 11001 in binary.
For a fraction we multiply by 2. The whole-number part of each product is the next bit.
Read these bits from top to bottom, and stop when the fraction becomes 0.
For octal or hexadecimal, divide by 8 or 16 instead. In hex, remainders 10 to 15 are written A to F.

body.en: To convert a *decimal* fraction to binary, multiply the fractional part by 2. The integer part of the product (0 or 1) is the next binary digit after the point. Repeat with the new fractional part until it becomes 0 or you have enough digits. Read the digits from top to bottom. For example, 0.375 × 2 = 0.75 (0), 0.75 × 2 = 1.5 (1), 0.5 × 2 = 1.0 (1), so $0.375 = (0.011)_2$.

problem.en: Convert (122)₁₀ to binary, octal and hexadecimal.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Convert (122)₁₀ to binary, octal and hexadecimal.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Convert 122 10 to binary, octal and hexadecimal.

Binary: 122 divided by 2 equals 61 r0, 61 divided by 2 equals 30 r1, 30 divided by 2 equals 15 r0, 15 divided by 2 equals 7 r1, 7 divided by 2 equals 3 r1, 3 divided by 2 equals 1 r1, 1 divided by 2 equals 0 r1; read upwards: 1111010.
Octal: 122 divided by 8 equals 15 r2, 15 divided by 8 equals 1 r7, 1 divided by 8 equals 0 r1; read upwards: 172.
Hexadecimal: 122 divided by 16 equals 7 r10 A, 7 divided by 16 equals 0 r7; read upwards: 7A.
So the answer is 122 10 equals 1111010 2 equals 172 8 equals 7A 16.

steps.en: 0.5 × 2 = 1.0 → integer part 1; the fraction is now 0, so stop.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Convert (0.375)₁₀ to binary.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Convert 0.375 10 to binary.
0.375 times 2 equals 0.75 gives integer part 0.
0.75 times 2 equals 1.5 gives integer part 1; continue with 0.5.
0.5 times 2 equals 1.0 gives integer part 1; the fraction is now 0, so stop.
So the answer is 0.375 10 equals 0.011 2.
